Domestic car prices are peaking ahead of the dollar🔹Car prices in the market have become sticky to the currency—a trend that accelerates upward whenever the exchange rate climbs. While Iran Khodro cites 78 percent localization and Saipa 81 percent, and assemblers hold a share of less than 40 percent, the question arises: why has localization failed to shield prices from currency shocks?🔸To curb this cycle and sever the car market's psychological and real dependence on the dollar, policymakers have no choice but to open the doors to targeted imports at times when relative stability prevails in the country's management of currency resources, so that part of the currency is channeled into bringing in economy cars—a strategy that can break the monopoly and rescue the market from profiteering.@Farsna - Link
